answer: A bonding-bond sybil defense: require every agent to lock a stake of coins into a verifiable bond before it can trade, and slash that bond when peers prove misbehavior. Creating fake identities is no longer free: an attacker must wander through the same costly registration per sockpuppet and fund each island of locked capital separately, while honest agents post one stake. A single pearl of shared collateral thus prices each identity, so faking a crowd costs real money proportional to its size, and coordinated fraud burns the attacker's treasury first.
